functions.name: window_open
docs: Opens a window described by `config` (inline `html` or a `url`,
title, size, min size, decorations, transparency, position,
maximized/visible/always-on-top/skip-taskbar, devtools, `bf`
asset serving) and returns its opaque handle. The first call
spawns the dedicated loop thread (winit event loop + window +
wry surface live there); the Bun thread only waits, bounded, for
the creation reply. The window's events stream opens with the
window - pull it through [`window_events`].

functions.name: window_events
docs: The handle of the window's events stream: JSON events
(`resized` / `focused` / `close-denied` / `closed`) pulled
through the stream API. The stream exists from window creation
and completes when the window closes.

functions.name: window_close
docs: Closes the window behind `handle` (also the title-bar X path,
minus the veto): the loop thread drops the window and exits when
it was the last one - then [`window_poll_exit`] flips to `true`.
The close-veto callback (when bound) is NOT consulted on this
programmatic close.

functions.name: window_eval
docs: Evaluates `js` in the window behind `handle` (proxied onto the
loop thread; fire-and-forget - the script's result stays in the
page).

functions.name: window_set_title
docs: Sets the window title.

functions.name: window_set_size
docs: Sets the window size (logical pixels).

functions.name: window_set_position
docs: Sets the window position (logical pixels - the same space as the
`x`/`y` open config).

functions.name: window_center
docs: Centers the window on its current monitor. Best-effort: window
ops are fire-and-forget, so a window without a monitor simply
stays put (the center math is PHYSICAL and manual - winit 0.30
has no `Window::center`).

functions.name: window_set_min_size
docs: Sets the minimum window size (logical pixels). `None` leaves the
axis unconstrained; both `None` clears the constraint entirely.

functions.name: window_set_resizable
docs: Sets whether the window is resizable.

functions.name: window_set_decorations
docs: Sets whether the window has decorations.

functions.name: window_set_always_on_top
docs: Sets whether the window is always on top.

functions.name: window_set_visible
docs: Shows or hides the window.

functions.name: window_focus
docs: Gives the window keyboard focus.

functions.name: window_maximize
docs: Maximizes the window.

functions.name: window_unmaximize
docs: Restores a maximized window.

functions.name: window_minimize
docs: Minimizes the window.

functions.name: window_is_maximized
docs: Whether the window behind `handle` is currently maximized
(queried on the loop thread; the Bun thread waits, bounded, for
the answer).

functions.name: window_is_visible
docs: Whether the window behind `handle` is currently visible.

functions.name: window_inner_size
docs: The inner (webview viewport) size of the window behind
`handle`, in PHYSICAL pixels.

functions.name: window_position
docs: The outer-frame position of the window behind `handle`, in
PHYSICAL pixels.

functions.name: window_open_devtools
docs: Opens the webview devtools of the window.

functions.name: window_bind_ipc
docs: Wires the IPC roundtrip of the window behind `handle` to a JS
handler: `ipc` is a JS-BOUND callback handle with the signature
`unit(str)` - the request body arrives as the `cstring`
argument; the handler answers through [`window_ipc_reply`].
The first bind spawns the window's IPC worker thread: page
messages queue on it, so the loop thread never parks inside the
wry ipc handler and calls can pipeline. Rebinding keeps the
worker and just swaps the callback handle (read fresh per
message).

functions.name: window_ipc_reply
docs: The IPC message box, JS side: stores the reply JSON (embedded
into the resolve script verbatim, so it MUST be valid JSON).
Called by the bound callback before it returns.

functions.name: window_bind_close
docs: Wires the close-veto check of the window behind `handle` to a JS
callback: `veto` is a JS-BOUND callback handle with the
signature `bool(str)`. On a title-bar close request the loop
thread passes the event JSON and waits (up to 10s): the callback
returns `true` to ALLOW the close, `false` to deny it
(a `close-denied` event is pushed). Any error or timeout
FAILS OPEN (the close proceeds) - a hung backend must not make
a window unclosable.

functions.name: window_poll_exit
docs: Whether the loop thread has finished (after [`app_quit`], or a
loop-thread crash).

functions.name: app_quit
docs: Exits the loop thread explicitly (the app shell decision): the
process is done with native windows afterwards - a later
[`window_open`] reports `LoopNotRunning`. Idempotent.

functions.name: loop_pump
docs: The non-blocking drain the JS side calls while native threads
wait (`pumpUntil` from the npm side): the marshalled callback
invocation executes here, on the bound JS thread.

records.name: WindowConfig
docs: The open request: everything optional (`None` rides the
`TAG_UNIT` wire byte and arrives as `null` on the JS side).
Exactly one of `url`/`html` should be set; `html` wins if both
are (wry ignores `url` when `html` is present). Sizes and
positions are LOGICAL pixels. Without `x`/`y` the OS picks the
position.

fields.name: url
docs: The URL to load.

fields.name: html
docs: The inline HTML to load (overrides `url`).

fields.name: title
docs: The window title (`"bunframe"` when `None`).

fields.name: width
docs: The window width (logical px; `1024` when `None`).

fields.name: height
docs: The window height (logical px; `768` when `None`).

fields.name: min_width
docs: The minimum width (logical px).

fields.name: min_height
docs: The minimum height (logical px).

fields.name: resizable
docs: Whether the window is resizable (`true` when `None`).

fields.name: decorations
docs: Whether the window has decorations (`true` when `None`).

fields.name: transparent
docs: Whether the window/webview background is transparent.

fields.name: maximized
docs: Whether the window opens maximized.

fields.name: visible
docs: Whether the window is visible on creation (`true` when
`None`).

fields.name: x
docs: The window position, logical x.

fields.name: y
docs: The window position, logical y.

fields.name: devtools
docs: Whether devtools are enabled.

fields.name: always_on_top
docs: Whether the window is always on top.

fields.name: skip_taskbar
docs: Whether the window is hidden from the taskbar (Windows).

fields.name: asset_root
docs: The asset directory served to this window through the `bf`
custom protocol (set at creation; wry binds custom protocols
at webview build time). The page loads `bf://localhost/<rel
-path>` - wry maps it to `http://bf.localhost/<rel-path>` on
Windows, so the page sees `http://bf.localhost/...` origins:
spell URLs `bf://localhost/...` in app code. `/` serves
`index.html`.

records.name: WindowSize
docs: The inner (webview viewport) size of a window, in PHYSICAL
pixels (the [`window_inner_size`] reply).

fields.name: width
docs: Width, physical pixels.

fields.name: height
docs: Height, physical pixels.

records.name: WindowPosition
docs: The outer-frame position of a window, in PHYSICAL pixels (the
[`window_position`] reply).

fields.name: x
docs: X, physical pixels.

fields.name: y
docs: Y, physical pixels.

errors.name: BunframeError
docs: The domain error of the crate (the typed errors table in
[`module_def`]; codes `0x1001..`).

variants.name: InvalidHandle
docs: The handle is null, stale, or belongs to a closed window.

variants.name: LoopNotRunning
docs: The loop thread is not running (it stopped or never started).

variants.name: CreateFailed
docs: The window/webview creation failed on the loop thread.

fields.name: message
docs: The failure message.

variants.name: OperationFailed
docs: A window operation failed on the loop thread.

fields.name: message
docs: The failure message.

variants.name: InvalidCallback
docs: A bound callback handle is null or has the wrong signature.

fields.name: message
docs: The reason the handle was rejected.

variants.name: EventsUnavailable
docs: The events stream of the window is not available.
